Criterion: Verify that servicing instructions are provided for all systems that require servicing; e.g., fuel, engine oil, hydraulic systems, landing gear struts, tires, oxygen, escape system, etc. Standard: All servicing information is provided for those subsystems that require servicing, including, as a minimum, fluid levels that require constant checking and servicing. Method of Compliance: Servicing information is verified by showing traceability from support analysis. Servicing information has undergone a quality assurance check, and the check and the content of servicing information have been verified by the government. References: JSSG-2000: 3.6.1, 3.6.2 JSSG-2001: 3.1.5 14 CFR 23.1501, 23.1529, 25.1501, 25.1503-25.1533, 25.1529, 25.1541, 25.1543, 25.1557, 25.1563; Part 23, Appendix G; Part 25, Appendix H, Instructions for Continued Airworthiness

Standard: Maintenance publications include servicing instructions for replenishing consumables depleted during normal operations (e.g., fuel, engine oil, hydraulic fluid). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine the maintenance publications to ensure they include servicing instructions derived from the RCM analysis servicing task requirements.
(2) Examine the artifacts that demonstrate contractor certification or contractor validation to ensure the maintenance publications have undergone a quality check for currency and accuracy IAW TO 00-5-3, Contractor Certification Process and Certification Requirements paragraphs for the Air Force; NAVAIR 00-25-604, Contractor Validation Plan and Validation paragraphs for the Navy; and DA PAM 25-40, Validation paragraphs for the Army. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct RCM analysis that meets SAE JA1011 to identify servicing task requirements. A4A MSG-3 Volume 1 and Volume 2 (previously ATA MSG-3) meet the intent of this MoC. Demonstration.
    (1) Perform air vehicle maintainability demonstrations to confirm the servicing instructions are complete, accurate, and can be performed as written without introducing AW hazards. Maintenance publications will receive updates to address maintenance issues discovered during maintainability demonstrations. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Demonstration.
    (2) Perform all air vehicle servicing procedures on production-configured hardware using government maintenance personnel to ensure servicing procedures do not introduce AW hazards.
